commands.name: Send_data_pack_1
commands.description: The motion command. Its length decides the control mode the driver enters: 8 bytes command a position with a speed and a current feedforward, 5 bytes a speed with a current feedforward, 2 bytes a current. Send 0 for a feedforward you do not use. A frame of any other length is ignored (the driver flags it as a wrong data length) but still answered.

forms.title: position setpoint with speed and current feedforward (position mode)
speed setpoint with current feedforward (velocity mode)

commands.name: Send_data_pack_PD
commands.description: Puts the driver in impedance (PD) mode and sets the position, speed and current feedforward of the PD loop, whose gains are KP and KD (Send_PD_Gains).

commands.name: Respond_data_pack_1
commands.description: The driver's answer to Send_data_pack_1 and Send_data_pack_PD: where the motor is, how fast it turns and the current it draws. The Python library stores them as `position`, `speed` and `current`.

commands.name: Send_PD_Gains
commands.description: Sets KP and KD, the gains of the impedance (PD) loop. Keep them with Send_Save_config.

commands.name: Send_Current_Gains
commands.description: Sets Kp and Ki of the PI current loop of Iq. The Id loop keeps its gains; over UART, `#Kpiq` and `#Kiiq` set both loops, and so do parameters 11 and 12.

commands.name: Send_Velocity_Gains
commands.description: Sets Kp and Ki of the PI velocity loop.

commands.name: Send_Position_Gains
commands.description: Sets Kp of the P position loop.

commands.name: Send_Limits
commands.description: Sets the speed limit and the current limit the loops may reach. From firmware 109 a negative value, or one that is not a number, is ignored, and the current limit stops at the driver's 2800 mA, as with `#Ilim`. Firmware 107 and older stored the current limit as it arrived. Never send more than the motor's rating.

commands.name: Send_Kt
commands.description: Sets the motor's torque constant Kt, which the driver uses to estimate torque from current.

commands.name: Send_Voltage_Limit
commands.description: Sets the voltage limit of the current loops (the same value as `#Vlim`), in mV. 0 means use the supply voltage. In the 104 release image (the source at tag V104 does not have it yet) and in every release from 105. From firmware 109 it takes 0 to 60000 mV, as parameter 17 does; a value outside is ignored.

commands.name: Send_Respond_Ping
commands.description: Asks the driver to answer with an empty frame, to see that it is on the bus.

commands.name: Send_Respond_Temperature
commands.description: Asks for the thermistor temperature. Meaningful only with the thermistor enabled (`#Term 1`).

commands.name: Send_Respond_Voltage
commands.description: Asks for the supply voltage.

commands.name: Send_Respond_Device_Info
commands.description: Asks for the driver's identity: hardware version, batch date and serial number from the EEPROM, and the firmware release (from firmware 105 on this is the build's own version; before, a value from the EEPROM).

fields.name: BATCH_DATE
fields.meaning: production batch, the lowest 8 bits of the stored value (24092024 after #Default is sent as 120)

commands.name: Send_Respond_State_of_Errors
commands.description: Asks for every error flag and the calibrated, activated, watchdog and product-lock states.

fields.name: driver_error
fields.meaning: the MOSFET driver reports undervoltage, thermal shutdown or overcurrent

fields.name: current_error
fields.meaning: reserved; never set by this firmware

fields.name: estop_error
fields.meaning: Send_ESTOP was received (from firmware 110 also #Estop over UART)

fields.name: wrong_product
fields.meaning: from firmware 109: this firmware is on the other product's board (the product lock) and drives nothing

commands.name: Send_Respond_Iq_data
commands.description: Asks for the measured Iq current.

commands.name: Send_Respond_Encoder_data
commands.description: Asks for the position and the filtered speed, as 32-bit values. Python attributes `position` and `speed`.

commands.name: Send_Respond_Kt
commands.description: Asks for the torque constant Kt the driver uses. Added in firmware 104.

commands.name: Send_Respond_Identity
commands.description: Asks what the drive is: the product, the tool it is built into, the firmware release, the hardware version, the pole pairs, whether it is calibrated, and eight flags. A host can check it before it commands or flashes a drive. Added in firmware 109. Python attributes `product_id`, `product_name`, `tool_id`, `firmware_version`, `identity_hardware_version`, `pole_pairs`, `identity_calibrated`, `identity_flags`.

fields.name: product
fields.meaning: 1 STEPFOC, 2 Spectral Micro: the firmware that answers

fields.name: tool_id
fields.meaning: parameter 1: 0 none, 1 SSG-48, 11-33 MSG, 200-254 your own

fields.name: pole_pairs
fields.meaning: the motor's pole pairs; 0 if outside 0-255

fields.name: gripper
fields.meaning: the driver is set up as a gripper (#Gripper 1)

fields.name: commutation_reversed
fields.meaning: calibration found the coils wired the other way round

fields.name: settings_block2
fields.meaning: the EEPROM has the bank settings block 2 lives in, so parameters 1-5 can be saved

fields.name: wrong_product
fields.meaning: this firmware is on the other product's board (the product lock) and drives nothing

fields.name: sense_zero_measured
fields.meaning: the current-sense zero was measured at start-up and is plausible

fields.name: cogging_saved
fields.meaning: the anti-cogging in use is the one saved in the EEPROM

fields.name: switching_zero_in_use
fields.meaning: the current-sense zero measured with the bridge switching is in use (parameter 46)

commands.name: Send_Respond_Telemetry
commands.description: Asks for the temperature, the supply voltage, both error bytes and the current in one frame, all from the same moment: one request instead of four. Added in firmware 109. The Python library fills the same attributes as the four separate answers.

fields.name: errors_1
fields.meaning: the error flags, as byte 0 of Send_Respond_State_of_Errors

fields.name: errors_2
fields.meaning: calibrated, activated, watchdog, wrong product, as byte 1 of Send_Respond_State_of_Errors

commands.name: Respond_Heartbeat
commands.description: The frame the driver sends on its own at the heartbeat interval (Send_Heartbeat_Setup); empty. Off by default. Any other frame the driver sends resets the heartbeat timer, so a driver that answers motion commands at a high rate never sends a heartbeat.

commands.name: Send_CAN_ID
commands.description: Gives the driver a new node ID, 0 to 13 (the firmware accepts up to 15, but the bootloader reserves 14 and 15: a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN). The driver answers to the new ID at once. The ID is kept over a power cycle only after Send_Save_config, and saving is also what copies it into the bootloader's board ID.

fields.name: ID
fields.meaning: 0 to 13 (14 and 15 are accepted but reserved by the bootloader)

commands.name: Send_ESTOP
commands.description: Stops the motor and raises the E-stop error, which stays until Send_Clear_Error.

commands.name: Send_Idle
commands.description: Puts the driver in idle mode: the motor coasts, or brakes when Send_Settings or `#Brake 1` asked for it.

commands.name: Send_Save_config
commands.description: Writes the current configuration (gains, limits, calibration, CAN ID, heartbeat, watchdog, gripper flag) to the EEPROM, and copies the CAN ID into the bootloader's board ID. From firmware 109 it also writes the tool id and the watchdog fallback (settings block 2), the anti-cogging set with its mode and scale, and the encoder table with its on/off flag, parameter 56 and the current-sense zero trims, each block with its own checksum; of the two large blocks only the 16-byte pages that changed are written. From firmware 110 it also writes the idle behaviour of Send_Settings (parameter 18). Not kept: the current loop bandwidth, and every parameter the parameter table marks as not kept. A drive stopped by the product lock writes nothing.

commands.name: Send_Reset
commands.description: Resets the driver. From firmware 104 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again; this is how a firmware update begins.

commands.name: Send_Clear_Error
commands.description: Clears the error flags and goes to idle; it also ends a watchdog hold or descend. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back. A calibration error is cleared only by calibrating.

commands.name: Send_Watchdog
commands.description: Sets the watchdog. The motion commands (Send_data_pack_1, Send_data_pack_PD, Send_gripper_data_pack) and the requests the driver answers (the Send_Respond_ remote frames, Send_Get_Parameter, Send_Buffer_Read) reset it; the other frames (Send_Parameter among them) and UART commands do not. When the time runs out the driver reports a watchdog error and does what the action byte says. 0 turns it off (the default). From firmware 109 the driver acts on the action byte, but only when the watchdog is the only active error: any other error gets the legacy response, the motor disabled and coasting. Hold and descend run for the fallback time (parameter 2, 2 s by default), then the after-action (parameter 5); they start only if the driver was in position, velocity, current, PD or gripper mode, otherwise the driver gives the legacy response and the motor coasts. Setting the time starts a fresh window, and a negative time means off. [The watchdog](../../06-operation/watchdog.md) explains each action. The setting is kept by Send_Save_config. The same values are parameters 6 and 7, which `#Par` reaches over UART: to turn off a saved watchdog, send 0 over CAN or `#Par 6,0`, and save.

fields.name: Action
fields.meaning: 0 legacy (the motor disabled, coasting), 1 hold the position, 2 brake (not current-limited), 3 coast, 4 descend at the fallback current and speed; other values act as 0

commands.name: Send_Heartbeat_Setup
commands.description: Sets the heartbeat interval in ms; 0 turns the heartbeat off (the default). Kept by Send_Save_config.

commands.name: Send_Settings
commands.description: Sets boolean settings that have no command of their own: a mask byte says which settings the frame touches, a value byte gives their new values; settings outside the mask are left alone. Bit 0 is the idle behaviour: 1 brake (phases shorted), 0 coast (the default). From firmware 110 Send_Save_config keeps it; on 109 the driver coasted again after a power cycle, as a driver still does that never saved it. Braking applies only in idle without an error; an error always disables the motor, which then coasts. The braking current is not limited, see Control modes. Added in firmware 107 (STEPFOC 107). The Python library has `Send_Settings(mask, value)` and, for this bit, `Send_Brake_Coast(brake)` from 1.21; 1.20 and older have no call for it.

commands.name: Send_Parameter
commands.description: Sets one parameter by its number (the [parameter table](#every-parameter)). Firmware 109 gives new settings a parameter number instead of a command ID of their own, since the identifier has room for only 64 command IDs. A value outside a parameter's range is clamped, replaced or refused as the table says; a number the firmware does not know, or a read-only one, is ignored. The driver does not answer: read the value back with Send_Get_Parameter. A value set this way lives in RAM until Send_Save_config, like every other setting; the table says which parameters Save keeps.

fields.name: Value
fields.meaning: the new value, in the parameter's unit; for the gains, limits and Kt (8-16, 20) a float's bit pattern

commands.name: Send_Get_Parameter
commands.description: Asks for the value in force of one parameter. The answer, Respond_Parameter, comes under ID 38, not 37: a host and a driver must never send data frames with the same identifier, because two sent at the same moment collide. Resets the watchdog. The Python library stores the value in `parameters[number]`.

commands.name: Respond_Parameter
commands.description: The answer to Send_Get_Parameter: the number and the value in force. For a number the firmware does not know the frame carries the number alone (1 byte; the Python library sets `unknown_parameter`). The gains, limits and Kt (parameters 8 to 16 and 20) travel as the bit pattern of an IEEE-754 float, the others as integers.

fields.name: value
fields.meaning: the value in force; a float's bits for 8-16 and 20

commands.name: Send_Buffer_Read
commands.description: Asks for entries of one of the drive's buffers: the capture, the histogram, the anti-cogging harmonics or table, or the encoder table. The driver answers with one Respond_Buffer_Data frame per entry (for the two tables, one per three values), sent from its main loop whenever a transmit mailbox is free, so a long read-out never holds up the control loop or other answers. A new request replaces one still in progress; count 0 cancels it. Entries past the end are not sent. Resets the watchdog.

fields.name: Kind
fields.meaning: 0 capture (up to 1024 samples: parameter 32 says how many), 1 histogram (256 bins), 2 anti-cogging harmonics (8 slots), 3 anti-cogging table (256 values), 4 encoder table (128 values)

fields.name: Count
fields.meaning: how many entries; 0 cancels a read-out

commands.name: Respond_Buffer_Data
commands.description: One entry of a buffer, the answer to Send_Buffer_Read. The first two bytes say which: the kind in the top three bits, the index in the other thirteen (kind × 8192 + index). The six bytes after them depend on the kind, as the table below the frame says.

fields.name: word_a
fields.meaning: capture: channel A; histogram: the count (unsigned); harmonics: the harmonic number (0 = slot unused); tables: entry index

fields.name: word_b
fields.meaning: capture: channel B; histogram: the sum's upper 16 bits; harmonics: a, the cosine term in mA; tables: entry index + 1

fields.name: word_c
fields.meaning: capture: channel C; histogram: the sum's lower 16 bits; harmonics: b, the sine term in mA; tables: entry index + 2 (0 past the end)

commands.name: Send_Buffer_Write
commands.description: Writes the anti-cogging set: kind 2 one harmonic slot per frame, kind 3 three table values per frame, in the Respond_Buffer_Data layout. Other kinds are ignored (the encoder table cannot be written), and so is a harmonic above 32. The set lives in RAM until Send_Save_config; switch it on with parameter 37. The driver does not answer.

fields.name: Word A
fields.meaning: kind 2: the harmonic (1-32, 0 = unused); kind 3: value at index

fields.name: Word B
fields.meaning: kind 2: a in mA; kind 3: value at index + 1

fields.name: Word C
fields.meaning: kind 2: b in mA; kind 3: value at index + 2

commands.name: Send_Sound
commands.description: Plays sound through the motor: a tone now, a queue of timed events, or samples. The sound is added to the output voltage, on the q axis by default (parameter 82), and only while the driver holds or moves (position, velocity, current or PD mode); idle or an error stops all of it. Up to 4 tones sound at once (channels 0 to 3), from 20 Hz to below 2500 Hz, half the control-loop rate. Loudness is given as a current: the driver turns it into a voltage with the coil's impedance at that pitch, so low and high notes sound alike. The total voltage is limited to parameter 81 (2000 mV by default; 0 refuses sound). Added in firmware 109. The driver does not answer; parameter 80 says what plays. The Python library wraps the operations as Send_Tone, Send_Sound_Stop, Send_Sound_Event, Send_Sound_Play, Send_Sound_Clear, Send_Samples_Play and Send_Samples_Stop.

fields.name: Operation
fields.meaning: 0 stop everything (tones, queue, samples); 1 a tone now; 2 add an event to the queue; 3 play the queue; 4 play the samples; 5 samples off, buffer cleared; 6 clear the queue (tones that sound keep sounding)

fields.name: A
fields.meaning: 1, 2: the pitch in Hz (2: 0 silences the channel); 4: the sample rate in Hz, at most the loop rate

fields.name: B
fields.meaning: 1, 2: the loudness in mA; 4: the voltage of a full-scale sample in mV

fields.name: C
fields.meaning: 1: the duration in ms, 0 = until stopped; 2: the wait in ms before the next event, 0 = the next one starts with it

commands.name: Send_Sound_Samples
commands.description: Appends 1 to 8 samples (signed 8-bit, one per byte, −127 to 127 = full scale) to the driver's 1024-place sample buffer, which holds 1023 samples. Samples that do not fit are dropped; parameter 80 says how many are buffered. Send_Sound with operation 4 plays them. Added in firmware 109. The driver does not answer.

forms.title: eight samples; a shorter frame carries fewer

commands.name: Send_gripper_data_pack
commands.description: The gripper command, for a driver set up as a gripper (`#Gripper 1`, saved). Position, speed and the current limit of the move, plus the activate, action and E-stop bits. A move is carried out only while the gripper is calibrated, activated and the action bit is 1. An empty frame (0 bytes) only asks for the state.

fields.name: Current
fields.meaning: current limit of the move in mA; from firmware 109 its magnitude is used and it stops at 2800 mA; see the gripper manual for the safe range; from firmware 110 the gripper's own limit, the driver's current limit (parameter 16) stays as set

fields.name: Release direction
fields.meaning: read by the firmware but not used

commands.name: Send_gripper_calibrate
commands.description: Starts the gripper calibration (the jaws find their end stops). Needed after every power-up. From firmware 110 each end is read under a light push and positions 0 and 255 lie a few ticks inside the two ends; this frame sent during a calibration starts it again from its first step. Parameter 93 gives the stroke found.

commands.name: Respond_Gripper_data_pack
commands.description: The driver's answer to Send_gripper_data_pack: position, measured current, and the state bits. Python attributes `gripper_position`, `gripper_current`, `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status`, `gripper_object_detection`, `gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error`, `gripper_calibrated`. The Python library 1.20 and older combine the two object-detection bits the wrong way round, so their `gripper_object_detection` reads 2 for an object found while closing and 1 for one found while opening; 1.21 and newer read them as the table says.

fields.name: gripper_action_status
fields.meaning: the action bit of the last Send_gripper_data_pack (1 after #Grippos); the driver never clears it, so it stays 1 after the move ends: the object detection tells when the move has ended

fields.name: gripper_object_detection
fields.meaning: bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit: 0 moving, 1 object detected while closing, 2 object detected while opening, 3 at the position

fields.name: gripper_timeout_error
fields.meaning: the driver's watchdog error: the CAN watchdog ran out
